headline: DevOps Engineer Salary in 2026: A Singapore Engineer's Benchmark Guide
metaDescription: Singapore engineers: US DevOps pay in 2026 — average salaries by experience level, top-paying employers and cities, and the skills that raise pay.

sections.content:
DevOps engineers remain among the better-paid roles in software, with 2026 postings on Indeed averaging around US$132,500 to US$133,350. Jobicy's October 2026 data puts the national average slightly lower at US$128,000, reflecting a broad mix of junior through senior roles. The gap between the two figures mostly comes down to how each source samples postings, but both point to a market comfortably above six figures.

For Singapore-based engineers, these US figures are the benchmark against which US remote offers and relocation packages get measured. Salary.com's September 2026 numbers show entry-level DevOps roles around US$82,000, mid-career engineers near US$134,000 and senior engineers around US$150,000 — the reference points that shape expectations when a US employer quotes a salary to a Singapore candidate.
sections.title: Average DevOps Engineer Salary in the US for 2026

sections.content:
Experience is the single biggest driver of DevOps pay. Jobicy's October 2026 breakdown puts junior engineers with 0 to 2 years of experience at US$76,300 to US$105,100, mid-level engineers with 3 to 5 years at US$104,400 to US$157,100, and senior engineers with 6 or more years at US$157,800 to US$242,200. Clearing the six-year mark roughly doubles the junior range.

The jump from mid to senior is where the money concentrates, because senior engineers own reliability decisions, architecture trade-offs and incident leadership that directly protect revenue. If you are early in your career, the fastest path upward is shipping production systems with real uptime responsibility rather than collecting tools on a resume.
sections.title: DevOps Pay by Experience Level

sections.content:
A small set of employers pay far above the market. Siemens leads Jobicy's October 2026 employer list at roughly US$301,600, followed by Grammarly at about US$267,000 and Dow Jones near US$265,000. These tend to be large enterprises or well-funded product companies where DevOps work sits close to revenue-critical systems.

Location matters almost as much as employer. Annapolis Junction, Maryland tops the city list at roughly US$176,000 to US$178,000 — a defence and government contracting hub — followed by Washington DC at US$142,000 to US$143,000, New York at US$139,000 to US$141,000, Chicago near US$137,700 and Dallas at US$136,000 to US$137,000. In San Francisco, lead DevOps roles reach a median near US$228,000.
sections.title: Highest-Paying Employers and Cities

sections.content:
The tools that command the biggest premiums are the ones behind modern cloud platforms: Kubernetes, Terraform and AWS dominate job requirements. Engineers who can design infrastructure as code, build reliable CI/CD pipelines and operate production clusters are consistently the hardest to hire, which is why those skills translate directly into higher offers.

Certifications help most when they validate skills you already use. The AWS Certified DevOps Engineer – Professional, the Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) and the Terraform Associate are the three credentials employers mention most often. Broader hybrid roles also pay well: platform-engineer and MLOps-hybrid positions earn roughly 20% above standard DevOps roles because they combine operations expertise with scarce specialist skills.
sections.title: Skills and Certifications That Raise Pay

sections.content:
DevOps is a competitive field to break into. Market data puts the supply-to-demand ratio near 1.9 to 1, meaning nearly two engineers compete for every open role — demand is strong, but so is the pipeline of candidates. Underlying demand is driven by ongoing cloud migration and the industry's reliance on CI/CD pipelines to ship software faster and more safely.

The practical takeaway is that junior engineers need differentiation. A public portfolio of real infrastructure work, contributions to open-source tooling, and hands-on experience with the core stack — Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS — moves applications to the top of the pile far more reliably than applying at volume.
